key_insight: The paper replaces heuristic smoothing in aneurysm surface reconstruction with a physics-informed neural network that enforces Laplace membrane equilibrium to preserve real high-curvature features while removing imaging artifacts.
engineering_relevance: This offers a geometry-aware, biomechanics-grounded reconstruction pipeline for patient-specific vascular models that can improve downstream rupture-risk assessment and clinical interpretation.
method: Encode aneurysm surfaces with B-spline geometry.
Train a PINN using a variational equilibrium loss (δΠ = 0) instead of an L-curve smoothing rule.
Use a manifold-consistent CNN ansatz to preserve closed-surface topology and suppress non-physical artifacts.
evidence_signal: On patient-specific clinical datasets, the method removed non-physical concave artifacts while preserving true geometric anomalies, and a neurosurgeon judged the resulting dome-apex risk map consistent with intraoperative observations.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality of imaging data and the fidelity of the physics prior, so overconstraining the model could still mask subtle but real anatomy if the equilibrium assumptions are violated.
paper_title: A physics-informed neural network for improving surface reconstruction of intracranial saccular aneurysms via variational membrane equilibrium
